steps.content: You can sense that everyone in the room is looking at you. There are appraising looks, grateful looks, distrustful looks, and looks of anticipation. You must control the whole situation here and now.
As a special representative, I had the opportunity to look around the dining hall of the Golstoy manor and to ask a few persons. And I found something interesting.

I had the powder in the jar tested. It was indeed the medicine for treating Mr. Golstoy's pains and other symptoms. It comes in white fine grains, very much like table sugar.

Putting two similar-looking substances in two similar jars on the same table, one is a drug, the other is table sugar... The cook and others in the manor wouldn't have allowed it, right? Even if it'd make it convenient to administer the medicine.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: But Miss Rita was in charge of the dining hall and she could decide where to put the jar. Isn't this proof that she had the chance to get her employer overdosed at any time?
I don't think it's Miss Rita who decided to put it there.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Who do you think was behind it then, sir?
steps.female_content: Who do you think was behind it then, miss?

steps.content: There was only one person in the manor who could do it. If this person wanted this jar of potentially dangerous substance placed there, no one else would say no.
Am I right, Mrs. Golstoy?

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: Hmm?

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: Are you saying I put it there?
Your mention of her name surprises Mrs. Golstoy.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: Are you joking?
If you ordered that something be put somewhere, no one would dare to disobey you.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: It doesn't make sense. You said it yourself. Someone could have consumed it by accident. Why would Mrs. Golstoy put herself in danger?
It's an order from the employer; the servants had to obey. There wasn't much they could do other than be careful not to use the wrong jar.
As for why Mrs. Golstoy did that, I guess it's because the medicine would be easier to access that way, and it would be easier for her to pin it on someone else.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: Are you accusing me of killing my husband?

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: Nonsense!

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Sir, have you given the submitted case file a close reading?
steps.female_content: Miss, have you given the submitted case file a close reading?

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Mrs. Golstoy was not in the dining hall at the time of her husband's death. She had finished eating and left, and she had even given her husband a kiss before she left.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Please enlighten us on how Mrs. Golstoy could possibly manage to poison her husband.
Mr. Fox, is the autopsy report... reliable?

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: ...Are you questioning the credibility of the best forensic experts in Eastside?
For the sake of justice and the truth, we must exhaust all possible avenues. Questioning the credibility of authorities should be one of them.
Fox chuckles, adjusting his glasses.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: I'm glad you remember something I said. But the reliability of the report has no bearing on this case, because there's no doubt that Mr. Golstoy was poisoned.
I beg to differ. The reliability of the report is of the essence here. Because I think Mr. Golstoy died of acidic drug-induced chronic toxicity, not acute toxicity.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: What difference does it make?

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Chronic toxicity can result from long-term consumption of higher-than-recommended doses of a certain drug. Miss Rita also had the opportunity to do this to Mr. Golstoy.
That's true. Miss Rita did have the opportunity.
But I've learned from Miss Rita that it was only recently that Mr. Golstoy decided to take the medicine for widespread body aches.
If it had been acute toxicity, Mr. Golstoy would have died sooner. If it had been chronic toxicity caused by this particular medicine, it would've taken longer for it to kill him.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: What's your point? According to your theory, Mrs. Golstoy should be in the clear. She couldn't have possibly gotten Mr. Golstoy to consume a medicine over a long period of time.

I found something on the dining-hall carpet. I had, um, one of my guys run a test on it to determine the components. For easier understanding, I'll use their commonly used names.
The mixture contains a personal lubricant and a bodily fluid. I'm sure you know what bodily fluid I'm referring to here.
Mrs. Golstoy flushes red at your words. She's been holding her head high, but now, out of embarrassment, she looks away quickly.
And it also contains some sort of acidic drug powder and medicated oil made from the acidic drug powder.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Sir, you may have accidentally revealed someone's big secret.
steps.female_content: Miss, you may have accidentally revealed someone's big secret.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: This might lead to another trial.

Cough, cough... My point is, isn't it possible that Mrs. Golstoy might have found a way to get Mr. Golstoy to absorb a high dose of the medicine on a daily basis while she was being intimate with him?
The table in the dining hall squealed loudly if you so much as touched it. I bet it must have been used quite a lot.
A couple of weeks, a month... that's enough time for chronic toxicity to kill a person.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Sir, that's a very unusual angle, very unusual indeed.
steps.female_content: Miss, that's a very unusual angle, very unusual indeed.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: But that still doesn't answer Mrs. Golstoy's question. Why would she want to kill her husband?

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Of course, you can take a page from my book and chalk it up to the dark side of human nature that predisposes human beings to evil deeds.
She might've acted out of self-interest, but that doesn't mean she's evil by nature.
Mr. Golstoy's first wife bore him only one heir, and this heir is mentally challenged. Any subsequent Mrs. Golstoy would have to bear him a healthy heir to secure her future in the Golstoy manor.
But physically, it might have become impossible for Mr. Golstoy to get his latest wife pregnant.
Mrs. Golstoy lived in constant fear of being deserted by her husband. On the other hand, a mentally handicapped kid was much easier to control.
Mrs. Golstoy lowers her head. You can't see her expression, but you notice how the brim of her hat trembles with her body.
You breathe a sigh, your eyes still on Mrs. Golstoy, half expecting to hear the sound of the judge's gavel.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Neat deduction, sir.
Clapping his hands, Mr. Fox leaves the plaintiff's table and goes over to stand before you.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Unfortunately, your deduction is flawed, from the very beginning.
You can't believe what you've just heard. Standing on the step behind the witness stand, you look down at Fox and catch glimpses of a shiny bead on his tongue as he talks.
At the plaintiff's table, Mrs. Golstoy looks up and smiles at you, her delicate face without a trace of panic.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Your entire argument, including the part about the motive, is based on my client being Mrs. Golstoy.
What do you mean?

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Legally speaking, my client, the Mrs. Golstoy you talked about, has no connection whatsoever with Mr. Golstoy.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: She asked me not to reveal this secret, unless it's absolutely necessary.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Because she was worried that if the secret was out, she would lose the right to take care of Golstoy Junior. What a kind-hearted lady she is.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Sir, Mrs. Golstoy has nothing to gain from Mr. Golstoy's death at all. According to the law, Mrs. Golstoy won't get anything out of all this, not even a dime.
steps.female_content: Miss, Mrs. Golstoy has nothing to gain from Mr. Golstoy's death at all. According to the law, Mrs. Golstoy won't get anything out of all this, not even a dime.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: The same can't be said for Miss Rita...
Fox changes his target and starts attacking Miss Rita, but he is still looking at you.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: As far as I know, you and Golstoy Junior are very close, right?

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: I believe that we should always consider the worst-case scenario when it comes to human nature...

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: On the one hand, we have a mother who doesn't have the law on her side. On the other hand, we have a young lady on whom a gullible heir to a large fortune relies.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: For this young lady, the only stumbling block was the patriarch of the family. Who do you think would control the manor if she removed the stumbling block and married the heir?
Miss Rita finally rises to her feet, tears welling up in her eyes, and starts shouting.

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: If... if you all think I did it, so be it.

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: But please don't leave Master Golstoy with Mrs. Golstoy.

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: He'll be... be tortured to death if he falls into their hands.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: Shut up. You're twisting the facts. Torture? Do you have proof?!

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: In any case, nobody is gonna believe the words of those who can't prove their own innocence.

Chief, Sinner Poffy's Emotion Test results came back normal. Her stats are at a stable, above-average level. Her social skills, cognitive function, and values all meet our standards for an ordinary person.
Miss Rita, are you bringing another charge against Mrs. Golstoy?
Taken aback by the idea, Rita is lost for words.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: What's the point of listening to what a murderer has to say? Let's...

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Let her finish.
Mr. Fox interrupts his client. His voice is deep but sounds somewhat irritated.
Mr. Fox knows what Rita has to say might hurt his client's case, but he still wants to hear it. For a second, your shackles stir. You sense a slight change in the psyche of the Sinner.
As if realizing he's spoken out of turn, Fox clears his throat and makes a gesture at Mrs. Golstoy that's meant to comfort her.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: There's nothing you can say that will change the indisputable fact, but we're kind, so go ahead and say your piece.
Miss Rita is clutching the hem of her dress, working up the courage.
Miss Rita's shaky voice ricochets off the walls of the spacious courtroom, echoing ever so slightly.

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: <size=32>Mr. Golstoy didn't like Master Golstoy, never treated him as a son. He hit Master Golstoy, shouted at him. He forbade him from eating at the same table, and even ordered him around like a servant. It had been like this ever since I came to the manor.</size>

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: Later on, I started bringing heated milk to Master Golstoy every night. I kept this from the others. If they... they saw Master Golstoy drinking milk in the dining hall, they'd take the milk away.

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: Mrs. Golstoy can't be trusted to take good care of Master Golstoy.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: That's funny. Why would I steal food from a dim-witted kid?

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: Besides, it's Mr. Golstoy who did that to him. What are you blaming me for?
Sometimes, silence is complicity, Mrs. Golstoy.
Golstoy Junior might have difficulty expressing himself, but I think it's necessary to give him a chance to speak his mind.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: You brought that kid here?!
In a moment of panic, Mrs. Golstoy, forgetting her manners, stands up, leaves the plaintiff's table, and points a finger at you.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: He's, um, not right in the head. His words can't be taken seriously.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: If that's the case, then we have nothing to worry about.
Fox returns to the plaintiff's table and places a hand on Mrs. Golstoy's shoulder. Mrs. Golstoy sits back down.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Let's give the floor to Golstoy Junior then. Everyone... everyone has a right to justice.
You know that Golstoy Junior, concerned about his friend Rita, has followed her to the court in secret.
He takes tentative steps, but every time he gets to the front, he becomes scared and runs back to hide behind Rita.
Don't be afraid.
Tell us what you know.

steps.speaker: Golstoy Junior
steps.content: I... I don't know... anything.

steps.speaker: Golstoy Junior
steps.content: Bad person hits me. The rat, rat, gray rat, it bites me...

steps.speaker: Golstoy Junior
steps.content: I'm not a bad boy. Don't let the gray rat bite me. It hurts... I'm not a bad boy, not a bad boy...

steps.speaker: Golstoy Junior
steps.content: Mommy, Mommy... It hurts, Mommy.

steps.speaker: Dignified Lady
steps.content: You never listen to me. You failed to do what you were told. You're a bad kid.

steps.speaker: Dignified Lady
steps.content: You're a bad kid. You deserve to be punished.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: I-I never laid a finger on you.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: Your father beat you, only because you didn't listen to him. I told you not to be naughty.

steps.speaker: Golstoy Junior
steps.content: You... you let the rat bite me.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: There's no rat in the manor!
With his elbows on the table, Fox listens attentively, wearing a frown on his face.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Master Golstoy, do you have evidence to back up what you've just said?

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: <size=32>If you do... then we shall go to hell together.</size>
Fox makes the remark in a light tone, as if it's directed at himself.

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: He must have. I often found bruises on him. We kept medicated oil at hand, and applied it on him every so often.
You walk over to the teenager and gently roll up his sleeve.
His arm is marked by faded bruises, a sign that he's been harmed before.

steps.speaker: Golstoy Junior
steps.content: The rat... bites my fingers... It hurts...

steps.speaker: Haggard Woman
steps.content: Thank you... Thank you...

steps.speaker: Haggard Woman
steps.content: Why thank you? Ah, because you showed us that he's a bad kid.

steps.speaker: Haggard Man
steps.content: You were right. The law is fair and just... He never listens to us, and he will never become a good kid.

steps.speaker: Haggard Man
steps.content: You won the case, which means our kid really is a bad seed. He has to be punished, has to atone for his sins... We all have sinned! That's why we've brought you here.

steps.speaker: Haggard Woman
steps.content: His wounds are proof of his sins, a punishment he deserves.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: No... You got it all wrong...

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: I was just... just trying to uphold justice. You got it all wrong...

steps.speaker: Haggard Woman
steps.content: He should go to hell.

steps.speaker: Haggard Man
steps.content: Yes, we should go to hell too.

steps.speaker: Haggard Woman
steps.content: Thank you, sir, thank you for letting us see the truth. Hell awaits us...

steps.speaker: Boy Covered in Scars
steps.content: Goodbye...

The wind whistles past a dilapidated building. In the moonlight, he hears the sound of several heavy objects hitting the hard ground in quick succession. It makes him feel suffocated. And then, he sees the scene of hell and makes for it.

Before he can get close, a gigantic hand grabs him and lifts him higher and higher to the sky until he reaches a place infused with bright light. The light burns him, crushes him, and lets him see the horrifying souls down below.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: <size=32>Argh...</size>

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: Mr. Fox, quit spacing out!

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: And get this over with.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Quiet!
Fox's voice is restrained but renders Mrs. Golstoy speechless. She is wide-eyed with astonishment.
Only you can sense it: Fox has activated his power.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Mrs. Golstoy, you kept it from me.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: You didn't tell me there's child abuse involved in this case!
Fox is still recovering from his last confrontation with you. Activating his power again gives him a splitting headache.

steps.speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
steps.content: I... I didn't abuse the kid...
With great effort, Mr. Fox raises his head and looks in your direction.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Let's put an end to all this.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Hell awaits me.
The atmosphere of the room has taken a sharp turn.
Mrs. Golstoy is no longer her demure self, now there's panic on her face. Restrained by Fox's power, she can do nothing but wait for a verdict to be delivered on her sins.
Golstoy Junior said, "The rat bites his fingers."
Of course there's no rat in the manor. But intellectually, he's just a small kid. We shouldn't take his words literally.
I noticed Mr. Golstoy's cigar cutter on the table in the dining hall. It's gray, and it was attached to a leather string.
You gently pick up Golstoy Junior's fisted hand, and open it. His fingers are dotted with long, thin scars.

Rita heated milk for him at night. No doubt that he stayed in the dining hall to drink it. The cigar cutter was a convenient tool. If someone found out he was hurt, it could be explained away by saying that he must have cut himself by accident.

<size=32>And fingertip wounds are hard to notice. As for why the perpetrator hurt him, my guess is that she wanted to, other than vent her anger, get Golstoy Junior's fingerprint on a document that stated his intention to transfer his inheritance rights.</size>
Mrs. Golstoy jumps to her feet, teeth grinding noisily. She keeps running her hand over her face, trying desperately to say something, to no avail.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: You and I are already deep in the mire. I couldn't care less about what your version of the truth really is.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: You wanted justice, you paid the right price, and I'd get you what you wanted. That's our deal.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: But you kept this child abuse business from me... You crossed a line that you should never have crossed.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: You shouldn't have done what you did to that kid.
Fox closes his eyes, and opens them again to look at you.
Your honor, it won't be difficult to track down the document. It's time to end this trial.
The trial ends. Mrs. Golstoy's scheme has been exposed. She's still shouting that Rita is guilty, but no one in the courtroom believes her.
Rita takes Golstoy Junior back to the Golstoy manor, to the messy dining hall. All the other servants are dismissed. Rita stands in the center of the dining hall, motionless like a statue.

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: Master, we're free, we're finally free...

steps.speaker: Golstoy Junior
steps.content: Rita...?

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: Hahaha... Hahaha...
Rita, who was all timid and shy in the courtroom, bursts out laughing, a high-pitched, blood-curdling laugh.

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: Stupid woman! Hahaha... Even luck was on my side!

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: It never occurred to her that your milk contained some of the powdered drug, or that the drink contained some of the medicated oil used for your fingertips.

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: That thing... it can kill you if you consume it.

Golstoy Junior stands there dumbfounded. He stares at his friend as her fair skin melts away, giving off the stench of something rotten. The molten skin then starts flowing like slow-moving black slime.
Her innocent, lovely face contorts out of shape, into a terrifying mask.

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: Those people, those rich people, they should all die... They have no right, no right at all, to enslave me, to make me their property, to make me feel invisible!

steps.speaker: Golstoy Junior
steps.content: Rita, you're so scary...

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: You too!
Rita twists her head around to look at her friend. There's something inhuman about her movements. And then she raises her hand.

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: An imbecile like you... You're lucky to have lived so long. You wouldn't have survived long in our household.

steps.speaker: Rita
steps.content: You're no use to me anymore. You never listen to me. Now die!

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: "Stop, Rita."
There's a red flash. Rita freezes, her hand inches from Golstoy Junior.
But her body continues mutating. A husky groan comes forth from deep in her throat, as if she's releasing all her pent-up emotional energy.
The man who's just walked out of the shadow, unsteady on his feet, gives Rita a second order.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: "Leave the manor. End yourself!"
Fox controls Rita, who's now turned into a monster, with his power-infused voice. She moves her hand away from Golstoy Junior slowly and places it on her own chest.
As she strides ahead, she knocks over Golstoy Junior on her path.

steps.speaker: Golstoy Junior
steps.content: Rita, where are you going? Rita, you don't want to play with me anymore?

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: That's not the Rita you know.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Say goodbye to her.
Not trusting his legs to support him, he leans back against the rickety table, which protests irritatingly.
Are you okay?

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Ha, I didn't expect that even with the support of the shackles, it'd still be so taxing on me... I guess I should refrain from using my power on you in the future.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: You knew she was infected with Mania, didn't you?
Yes, I realized that when I first talked to her.
You were not the reason I got involved in the trial; she was. Her M-value was higher than normal.
You pick Golstoy Junior up from the floor, sit him down in one of the chairs, and call the city hall, so that he can be taken care of.
All right then. Mr. Fox, you've assisted the MBCC in handling the murderer and Corruptor in the case of the Eastside Golstoy manor. You'll not be punished for leaving the MBCC without permission.
Mr. Fox chuckles at your words.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Are you abusing your power?
No. If this sort of thing happens again, I won't let you leave the MBCC premises ever again.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Hahaha... Whatever you said. You're the winner.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: I wouldn't have agreed to take on this case if I had learned more details about it.
Really? That's interesting. I guess this case was not quite to your taste then, Mr. Fox. Right?
Is it because there's child abuse involved in this case?
Fox narrows his eyes, and looks you up and down, as if seeing you for the first time.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: You seem to know more about my past than I expected.
I told you I knew a lot about you when we first met. I'm the Chief of the MBCC; it's my job to dig into the past of every detained Sinner.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: Hahaha... You're right, it is because there's child abuse involved in the case. Because of me, a kid, the plaintiff in an abuse case, jumped to his death.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: The sad thing wasn't that I couldn't follow him and meet the same hellish fate, because I had been restrained, but that I gained my ability because of it, an ability that allowed me to stand on the side of justice, albeit a distorted version of it.
You became a Sinner.
Then why did you keep...

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: I needed more sins, more unforgivable sins, so that my final punishment would be more... horrific.
Mr. Fox stands up, his reddish eyes gleaming in the dimness, like those of a predator locking onto its prey.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: I used to think that everything in this world could be manipulated and exploited, and that's why I had won so many victories.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: But I had no peace of mind, until I met you.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: I've been waiting for the person who'll mete out my sentence.

steps.speaker: Mr. Fox
steps.content: If I really am a bad seed, then I hope you'll be the one who sends me down to hell.
